skill.name: skill-template
skill.description: Template for building production-grade DocEngineering skills with structured instructions, validation steps, and portable assets.
skill.summary: Build consistent DocEngineering skills with a reusable workflow template.
skill.author: 64andrewwalker

security_audit.summary: All five static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code formatting, not executable shell calls. I found no prompt injection, data exfiltration, or hidden execution intent in SKILL.md or scripts/run.py. The template declares Python Bash access, but the reviewed content uses it only for a simple self-test entrypoint.

static_findings.snippet: - Prefer relative paths via `{baseDir}` for portability.
1. **Scout**: Use `Grep`/`find` to locate only the relevant files.
- Define a strict output format (Markdown template in `{baseDir}/assets/` and/or JSON schema).
- If any hard gate fails, return `EXIT_BLOCKED` and list blockers.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 20 contains Markdown inline code around {baseDir}. It is documentation for relative paths, not Ruby backtick execution or a shell command.
Line 24 uses Markdown inline code for tool names Grep and find in a workflow step. It does not execute a command or interpolate user input.
Line 26 uses Markdown inline code to reference the scripts directory. It recommends deterministic scripts but contains no executable backtick expression.
Line 31 formats a relative asset path as Markdown inline code. This is prose documentation and not shell execution.
Line 36 formats the EXIT_BLOCKED status token as Markdown inline code. It is an output convention, not a command execution pattern.

content.user_title: Create DocEngineering Skills From a Template
content.value_statement: Building a reusable AI skill can create inconsistent instructions and weak validation. This template gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured workflow for skill creation.
actual_capabilities: Defines a frontmatter manifest with name, description, and allowed tools.
Guides agents through scout, analyze, execute, and verify steps.
Encourages relative paths through {baseDir} for portable skill assets.
Includes a Python entrypoint that supports a --test self-check.
Documents error handling for missing inputs and hard gate failures.
limitations: It is a template, so it needs customization before production use.
It does not include a finished output schema or assets directory.
It depends on authors to add domain-specific tests and validation.
It allows only Python Bash commands by default.

use_cases.title: Bootstrap a New Skill
use_cases.description: Start from a documented folder structure before adding domain instructions, assets, and validation scripts.

use_cases.title: Standardize Agent Workflow
use_cases.description: Give contributors a shared scout, analyze, execute, and verify process for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

use_cases.title: Teach Skill Design
use_cases.description: Use the template to explain manifests, allowed tools, output rules, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this template to create a basic documentation skill. Ask for missing inputs before changing files.

prompt_templates.title: Customize the Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt this skill template for my workflow. Update the scout, analyze, execute, and verify steps for the domain.

prompt_templates.title: Add Validation Gates
prompt_templates.prompt: Extend this template with validation gates, expected outputs, and failure handling for a production skill.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare for Marketplace Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this customized skill against marketplace expectations. Identify missing metadata, risky tools, and unclear instructions.

output_examples.input: Create a skill for release note writing.
output_examples.output: A skill outline with focused instructions, supported tools, verification steps, and release note output expectations.

output_examples.input: Check whether my customized skill is ready for review.
output: A readiness summary covering metadata, allowed tools, workflow clarity, and validation coverage.
A short blocker list for missing inputs or failed checks.

output_examples.input: Add a self-test to the template.
output_examples.output: A simple validation plan that runs the existing entrypoint and reports pass or blocked status.

best_practices: Replace placeholder instructions with a narrow workflow for one clear domain.
Keep allowed tools limited to the commands needed by the finished skill.
Run the self-test and domain validation before publishing the skill.
anti_patterns: Publishing the template unchanged as a finished user workflow.
Adding broad shell access without a clear validation requirement.
Skipping output rules and leaving users to infer the result format.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps authors create structured DocEngineering skills with clear instructions, validation steps, and failure handling.

faq.question: Is this a finished workflow?
faq.answer: No. It is a starting template that needs domain instructions, assets, and tests before production use.

faq.question: Which AI tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it run external commands?
faq.answer: The skill declares Python Bash access, and the included script only provides a simple self-test entrypoint.

faq.question: What should I customize first?
faq.answer: Start with the skill description, domain workflow, expected output format, and validation checks.

faq.question: Can teams use it for standards?
faq.answer: Yes. Teams can use it to standardize manifests, allowed tools, workflow steps, and review expectations.
